title: Audit Your Spending
blurb: Find patterns in your spending without judging yourself.
cards: Review recent transactions over a representative period. Group them into essentials, flexible spending, savings and debt. Hide account numbers and other private details if you take notes.
Check for forgotten subscriptions, costs that rose, and categories that regularly exceed your plan. The goal is to find one change that fits your life.
Pick the most practical next step.
A subscription you have not used in months
Three small purchases that happen every day
Recurring patterns and changed bills are useful to review. A necessary one-off cost is not a personal failure.
What is the purpose of a spending audit?
Prove that every purchase was wrong
Spot patterns and choose practical adjustments
An audit gives you information to improve your plan, without shame.
You find one category is consistently too low. What next?
Raise it to a realistic amount and adjust elsewhere
A budget should reflect real life. Adjust the plan using what you learned.
example: A $9 subscription you no longer use costs $108 over a year. Reviewing recurring payments can reveal changes that are easy to miss month to month.
